argument: Pressure must be carried by the surface itself: nodes near the path need to compact, rise, tilt, and change grain while the crease follows the pressure path. A colored band over an unchanged mesh is not an archive.

With labels, controls, readout, and pressure witnesses hidden, a viewer should find one continuous topographic object rather than a population of angular marks. If it reads as a decorated grid, the medium switch fails.

A drag must be causally different from a click: path shape and pressure must alter the surface geometry. Enter/Space may provide a deterministic equivalent, and lifting only the latest pressure must restore the exact preceding topography.

Compaction is an easy metaphor. Delete v014 if the crease is decorative, if edge-to-edge pressure produces no material displacement, if pressure has no consequence beyond colour, or if prose carries more force than the blind object can show.
